After completing J1—J3 independently, record which fields are easily missed, whether the recalculation can be explained, and whether the handover is specific, then investigate one real course or job; keep a note that the paper work involved no practical operation.

The core object is oil and gas well power pumps and auxiliary equipment, with the purpose of making oil or gas flow in the well; general non-wellhead pumps 53-7072 and drilling 47-5012 are different statistical tasks.

Monitor the running status of pumps and flow lines and watch for anomalies such as gas and liquid leaks; the actual observation and handling methods are determined by site procedures and trained duties.

Operation monitoring focuses on pump and pipeline status, and measurement records focus on output and its basis. The tasks may be carried out in the same job, but a correct formula cannot replace site status and safety confirmation.

Wellhead pumpers operate power pumps and auxiliary equipment within U.S. 53-7073.00 to make oil or natural gas flow from oilfield wells. The work includes observing pump and pipeline status, measuring production, monitoring gauges, operating per specified tasks, performing upkeep, and keeping records. It is not a general term for all pump stations, drilling, or reservoir research jobs; Chinese oil production and wellhead jobs must be compared by equipment and actual task, and operation, repair, engineering design, and emergency authority are checked separately.
Manage geothermal power facility operations and maintain monitoring equipment.
Design and improve oil and gas extraction methods and provide drilling technical advice.
Assemble derrick equipment and operate drilling mud circulation pumps.
Set up or operate drilling rigs for oil and gas exploration and core sampling.

Use fictional well numbers and cumulative readings to practice document checking, then check formal training, site qualifications, and specific jobs.

subject.name: Wellhead Pumpers
subject.summary: Wellhead pumpers operate power pumps and auxiliary equipment within U.S. 53-7073.00 to make oil or natural gas flow from oilfield wells. The work includes observing pump and pipeline status, measuring production, monitoring gauges, operating per specified tasks, performing upkeep, and keeping records. It is not a general term for all pump stations, drilling, or reservoir research jobs; Chinese oil production and wellhead jobs must be compared by equipment and actual task, and operation, repair, engineering design, and emergency authority are checked separately.
